const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/horizontal-sketch-luna.md <<'EOF'
Usage sketch

```svelte
<CategoryWheel
  options={updateCategories}
  selected={view.category}
  onselect={selectCategory}
  label="Latest declarations"
  orientation="horizontal"
/>
```

Keep the prop optional; omitted means current square wheel. Define `CategoryWheelOrientation = "vertical" | "horizontal"` in `ranking-types.ts`, default `vertical`. For horizontal mode the component owns its 284×142 canvas and renders two native 284×142 button hit targets, each clipped to its half. `updateCategories` supplies the horizontal sector paths and label coordinates: MPs top, Companies bottom. Retain option IDs and accents as the semantic source; no duplicated category allowlist. Labels stay upright because the component lays them out in the unrotated canvas. Keep SVG focus outline tied to focused option and `--focus-color` neutral.

Rationale

Choose native horizontal geometry over rotating the square canvas and counter-rotating labels. Rotation makes bounding boxes and hit regions harder to reason about and tends to require per-label transforms; native bounds preserve reliable full-half button targets and simpler responsive sizing. The tradeoff is maintaining a second geometry set for this presentation. Scope orientation explicitly to rendering geometry; selection, order, category identity, and existing square callers remain intact. Add no visible copy. Ensure outer aspect ratio follows orientation; preserve existing default square dimensions and behavior.
EOF
